question: 大学の奨学金(しょうがくきん)に ＿応募＿ した。

question: 試験の成績(せいせき)が ＿発表＿ された。
source_explanation:
発表 is read はっぴょう because 発 undergoes a sokuon contraction to はっ and 表 takes the on-yomi ひょう, voiced to ぴょう after the small っ.
発表 (はっぴょう) means "announcement" or "presentation." The reading requires understanding two phonological rules at once. First, 発 (はつ/ほつ) has an on-yomi はつ, but when it precedes a syllable beginning with ひ/は, the つ contracts into a sokuon っ: はつ + ひょう → はっひょう → はっぴょう. Second, after the glottal stop っ, the following consonant voices: ひょう becomes ぴょう. So the full chain is: は + っ + ぴょう = はっぴょう. question: 1 今年の夏は、 ＿過去＿ 十年間で一番の暑さだったそうだ。
source_explanation:
過去 is read かこ because 過 takes on-yomi か and 去 takes on-yomi こ, forming the short compound meaning "the past."
過去 (かこ) means "the past" — time that has already elapsed. Both kanji take their on-yomi: 過 (か) = to pass, and 去 (こ) = to go away/leave. Together they describe time that has passed and gone. The sentence says: "This summer, the heat is apparently the worst in the past ten years." 過去十年間で一番の暑さ = "the hottest in the past ten years." question: 2 あと５分で東京駅に ＿到着＿ します
source_explanation:
到着 is read とうちゃく — 到 reads とう and 着 reads ちゃく, meaning "arrival".
到着 (とうちゃく) = arrival. 「あと5分 (ふん) で東京駅 (とうきょうえき) に到着 (とうちゃく) します」 — "We will arrive at Tokyo Station in 5 minutes." 到 reads unvoiced とう (not voiced どう).
✗ とうつく: correct とう for 到 but kun-yomi つく for 着. In 到着, 着 takes on-yomi ちゃく.
✗ どうつく: voices 到 to どう (wrong) and uses kun-yomi つく for 着 (wrong).
✗ どうちゃく: correct ちゃく for 着 but voices 到 to どう (wrong).
例: 飛行機 (ひこうき) は30分 (さんじゅっぷん) 遅 (おく) れて到着 (とうちゃく) した。 — The airplane arrived 30 minutes late.

question: 3 公園の木の枝を ＿折って＿ はいけません。
source_explanation:
折って is read おって, meaning "break off / snap" — breaking branches in a park is prohibited.
折る (おる) means "to break off," "to snap," or "to fold." Its te-form 折って (おって) is used in compound instructions or descriptions. The sentence says: "You must not break 折って (おって) the branches of park trees." 公園の木の枝を折ってはいけません = "Do not snap branches off park trees" is a public rules sign. The kanji 折 uses the kun-yomi お in the transitive verb form: 折る (おる, you snap something). The intransitive counterpart is 折れる (おれる, it snaps by itself). question: 4 インターネットで最新の ＿情報＿ をチェックした。
source_explanation:
情報 is read じょうほう — 情 reads じょう and 報 reads ほう, meaning "information".
情報 (じょうほう) = information/data. 情 (じょう) = feelings/circumstances, 報 (ほう) = to report. 「インターネットで最新 (さいしん) の情報 (じょうほう) をチェックした」 — "I checked the latest information on the internet."
✗ じゅうほう: じゅう for 情 is wrong. 情 reads じょう. じゅう belongs to 十 (ten) or 重 (heavy).
✗ じょうほ: shortens ほう to ほ. 報 reads ほう (long vowel), not ほ.
✗ じゅうほ: wrong じゅう for 情 and wrong ほ for 報.
例: 最新 (さいしん) の情報 (じょうほう) はウェブサイトで確認 (かくにん) できます。 — You can check the latest information on the website.

question: ＿ものがたり＿ は誰でも知っている。
source_explanation:
ものがたり is written 物語 — 物 means "thing" and 語 means "story / language", together meaning "a story / tale".
物語 (ものがたり) = a story, tale, or narrative. 物 (もの) = thing/matter, 語 (がたり) = story/telling (voiced from かたり by rendaku). Together: a telling of things/events — a story. The sentence says 「その物語 (ものがたり) は誰 (だれ) でも知 (し) っている」 — "Everyone knows that story." 物語 covers fairy tales, novels, historical narratives, and legends. Note the rendaku: 語 (かたり) voices to がたり in this compound.
✗ 物化: 化 (か, transformation/化学=chemistry) instead of 語 (かたり/がたり, story). 物化 is not a standard compound meaning "story".

question: 11 大学では ＿ほうりつ＿ を勉強ました。
source_explanation:
ほうりつ is written 法律 — 法 (law/method) + 律 (rule/regulation).
法律 (ほうりつ) means "law" in the legal sense — the body of rules governing society. Both kanji use on-yomi: 法 (ホウ, law/method) + 律 (リツ, rule/rhythm). Together they refer to enacted law (statutes). The sentence 「大学では法律を勉強しました」 means "I studied law at university." The trap is distinguishing 法 (ホウ) from 方 (ホウ), and 律 (リツ) from 立 (タツ). question: 12 いつか京都をゆっくり ＿かんこう＿ したい。
source_explanation:
かんこう is written 観光 — 観 (view/observe) + 光 (light/scenery).
観光 (かんこう) means "sightseeing" or "tourism". Both kanji use on-yomi: 観 (カン, to view/observe) + 光 (コウ, light/radiance — here extended to mean the brilliant sights of a place). The sentence 「いつか京都をゆっくりかんこうしたい」 means "Someday I want to take my time sightseeing in Kyoto." The test distinguishes 観 from 歓 (also カン, but meaning "joy/welcome") and 光 from 察 (サツ, investigate). question: 13 当日、この ＿けん＿ を忘れないようにしてください。
source_explanation:
けん (ticket/voucher) is written 券 — the speaker is told not to forget this ticket on the day.
券 (けん) means "a ticket" or "a voucher". The sentence 「当日、このけんを忘れないようにしてください」 means "Please make sure not to forget this ticket on the day of the event." The on-yomi ケン is the standard reading for 券 when it stands alone or at the end of a compound. It appears in: 入場券 (にゅうじょうけん, admission ticket), 乗車券 (じょうしゃけん, train ticket), 商品券 (しょうひんけん, gift voucher). source_explanation:
なみだ is written 涙 — the kanji for "tears".
涙 (なみだ) means "tears" — the liquid produced when crying. The sentence 「なかなかなみだが止まらなくて困りました」 means "The tears just would not stop, which troubled me." Among the four options, 涙 is the only kanji meaning tears. Its on-yomi is ルイ (as in 感涙 かんるい, tears of emotion), but in everyday speech and in this context the kun-yomi なみだ is always used. question: 9 やくそくを ＿まもる＿ ことは大切だ。
source_explanation:
まもる is written 守る because 守る means "to keep / to protect", fitting the importance of keeping a promise.
守る (まもる) = to keep, to protect, to observe (a rule or promise). The sentence says 「やくそくをまもることは大切 (たいせつ) だ」 — "It is important to keep a promise." 約束を守る (やくそくをまもる, to keep a promise) is a set phrase in Japanese. The kanji 守 contains 宀 (roof) on top and 寸 (measurement) below — the image of carefully guarding what is under your roof.

question: 10 今、この ＿しゅうかんし＿ が一番売れている。
source_explanation:
しゅうかんし is written 週刊誌 because 刊 means "publication issue" and 誌 means "magazine," giving the compound its precise meaning of "weekly magazine."
週刊誌 (しゅうかんし) means "weekly magazine" — a periodical published once a week. The three kanji each carry a specific meaning: 週 (しゅう) = week, 刊 (かん) = publication issue or print run, 誌 (し) = magazine or periodical. question: 11 今日はこれから友達と旅行の ＿そうだん＿ をします。
source_explanation:
そうだん is written 相談 because 相 means "mutual" and 談 means "to talk/discuss," together meaning "consultation" or "discussing a matter together."
相談 (そうだん) means "consultation," "discussion," or "talking something over with someone." Both kanji take their on-yomi: 相 (そう) = mutual/each other/appearance, and 談 (だん) = to talk/discuss. Together they describe a mutual conversation about a topic — two people talking it through. question: 12 わたしは体力には ＿じしん＿ があります。
source_explanation:
じしん is written 自信 — 自 (self) + 信 (confidence/belief).
自信 (じしん) means "self-confidence" or "confidence in oneself". Both kanji use on-yomi: 自 (ジ, self) + 信 (シン, belief/trust). Together the word means "trust in oneself". source_explanation:
あたためました is written 温めました because 温 means "to warm up" something — here, warming milk in a microwave.
温める (あたためる) means "to warm up" or "to heat" — bringing something to a comfortable warm temperature, often food or drink. Its past polite form 温めました (あたためました) describes the completed action. question: 14 この製品の ＿げんりょう＿ はすべて輸入しています。
source_explanation:
げんりょう is written 原料 because 原 means "original/raw" and 料 means "material/fee," together meaning "raw materials."
原料 (げんりょう) means "raw materials" or "ingredients" — the base substances used to manufacture a product. Both kanji take their on-yomi: 原 (げん) = original/raw/source, and 料 (りょう) = material/fee. Together they describe original source materials. question: みんなで話し合って、問題を ＿かいけつ＿ した。
source_explanation:
かいけつ is written 解決 — 解 means "to untangle/solve" and 決 means "to decide/resolve".
解決 (かいけつ) = to resolve/solve a problem. 解 (かい) = to untangle/dissolve (理解, りかい), 決 (けつ) = to decide/resolve (決める, きめる). 「みんなで話 (はな) し合 (あ) って、問題 (もんだい) を解決 (かいけつ) した」 — "We discussed and resolved the problem."
✗ 改決: 改 (かい, to reform) instead of 解 (かい, to untangle). Both read かい but different meanings. 改決 is not a real word.
✗ 改結: 改 (reform) and 結 (けつ, to bind). Binding is opposite of resolving. Not a real word.
✗ 解結: correct 解 but wrong 結 (to bind) instead of 決 (to decide). 解結 is not a real word.

question: 昨日は残業で ＿きたく＿ が遅くなった。
source_explanation:
きたく is written 帰宅 because 帰 means "to return home" and 宅 means "one's home/residence," forming the compound for "arriving home."
帰宅 (きたく) means "arriving home" or "returning home" — specifically, the act of coming back to one's residence at the end of a day. Both kanji take their on-yomi: 帰 (き) = to return, and 宅 (たく) = one's home/residence. Together they describe returning to one's own home. The sentence says: "Yesterday, because of overtime, my arrival home 帰宅 (きたく) was late." 案内 (あんない) means "to guide" or "to show around". The kanji 案 (アン) carries the idea of a plan or a proposal; 内 (ナイ) means "inside" or "within". question: 9 東京は ＿げんざい＿ 午後３時です。
source_explanation:
げんざい is written 現在 because 現 means "present/current" and 在 means "to exist/to be present," together meaning "right now / the present time."
現在 (げんざい) means "the present time" or "currently" — it is used to indicate the current moment or current state of affairs. source_explanation:

source_explanation:

育てる (そだてる) means "to raise," "to bring up," or "to nurture" — caring for a child, animal, or plant until it grows. question: 米の輸出量が去年の2 ＿ばい＿ になった。

question: 昨日の夕方、この辺りで ＿ていでん＿ があった。
source_explanation:

停電 (ていでん) means "power outage" or "blackout" — electricity stopping or being cut. Both kanji take their on-yomi: 停 (てい) = to stop/halt/suspend, and 電 (でん) = electricity. source_explanation:
にげる is written 逃げる — the cat runs away when the speaker tries to touch it.

question: この町は、昔から ＿商業＿ が盛んだった。

source_explanation:

The te-form 覚えて (おぼえて) here connects with いません to form the negative ongoing state: 「メールアドレスは覚えていません」 — "I have not memorized the email address." question: 新しいサービスの ＿広告＿ はまだできていません。
source_explanation:
広告 is read こうこく — 広 reads こう and 告 reads こく, meaning "advertisement".
広告 (こうこく) = advertisement. 「新 (あたら) しいサービスの広告 (こうこく) はまだできていません」 — "The advertisement is not ready yet."
✗ ほうこく = 報告 (report). 報 (ほう) ≠ 広 (こう).

question: 今朝から ＿は＿ が痛いんです。
source_explanation:
は (tooth) is written 歯 — this morning the speaker has a toothache.
